body:
Implement slice 5 of docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md: finish the **enforcing tier** of context-rot handoff adapters. The spec names four enforcing harnesses — Pi, OpenCode, CC, Codex. Slice 4 (T157, PR #476) shipped CC. This ticket ships the remaining three (Codex, OpenCode, Pi) and promotes the harness-agnostic half of the CC adapter into `@adlc/context-handoff` so no harness forks D1-D3, the deny-set, or the protected-path list.

This ticket does NOT wire the advisory/manual tiers (Cursor, Gemini/Antigravity, Copilot — slice 6) and does NOT add Proven CI (slice 7).

Binding design: docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md and .adlc/specs/context-rot-handoff.md — do not weaken D1-D3, `authorized()`, band edges, or the CLI contracts. Reference implementation to mirror: plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/{handoff-gate,handoff-resolve,adlc-hook}.mjs and plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs.

=== SEQUENCE (land in this order) ===

**Step 1 — promote the shared adapter core into the package.**
Move the harness-agnostic helpers currently in plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/handoff-gate.mjs into `@adlc/context-handoff` and export them from lib/index.mjs: `evaluateHandoffPreToolUse`, `isProtectedHandoffPath`, `isHandoffMutatingShell`, `resolveHandoffSessionId` (the generic session-id-candidate resolver: first candidate passing `isSafeSessionId`, including a transcript-path stem), and `HANDOFF_MUTATING_SUBCOMMANDS`. Behaviour must be byte-for-byte equivalent: the slice-4 CC contract test is a frozen rail here and must pass **unmodified** against the delegating CC hook. No existing test in packages/context-handoff/test/ asserts the index export surface, so adding exports does not require editing a frozen rail.

plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/handoff-gate.mjs keeps only the harness-specific bits (the Claude Code payload readers `bashCommandFromInput` and the CC-shaped `resolveSessionId` wrapper) and calls the promoted core through the loaded `api`; the generic helpers must not survive as a second copy there.

New package tests go in a NEW directory `packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/` — `packages/context-handoff/test/**` and `cli-test/**` are frozen rails and must neither gain nor lose files. Wire the new directory into the package's test script the same way `cli-test/` is wired.

Adapters call these off the dynamically-loaded `api` namespace (the object returned by the per-plugin resolver), never via a static top-level `import` from a hook script: a static import of a workspace package from a hook file turns an unresolvable package into a module-load crash for **every** hook mode, which would fail closed on a repo that never opted into handoff. Keep the existing CC behaviour — package unresolvable ⇒ deny for `handoff` mode only.

**Step 2 — Codex (subprocess hooks, mirrors CC).**
Add `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-handoff-gate.mjs` wired in plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/hooks.json as a PreToolUse hook on the existing mutation matcher (apply_patch/write/edit/multi_edit/Bash/Shell/exec/exec_command/write_stdin/multi_tool_use.parallel). Codex hook scripts cannot resolve npm packages from their install dir, so copy plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/handoff-resolve.mjs verbatim to plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/handoff-resolve.mjs and pin the two with a drift test (same KEEP-IN-SYNC pattern packages/core/test/shell.test.mjs uses for shell.mjs). Deny = `process.exit(2)` with the reason on stderr, matching adlc-rails-guard.mjs / adlc-build-gate.mjs in the same directory. Session identity: payload `session_id` if present, else the `transcript_path` stem (document the chosen source in the hook header). Depth/bytes signals: the same transcript-derived observation the Codex build-gate already performs, fed to `evaluateBands` — no new threshold literals. The plugin's `files` allowlist already ships `hooks/*.mjs`, so no packaging change is needed for the new hook.

**Step 3 — OpenCode (in-process plugin).**
Wire the handoff gate into `tool.execute.before` in plugins/adlc-opencode/index.mjs, alongside the existing rails-guard and build-gate checks, using the established `deny()` path (notify + throw to abort the tool call). Session identity: `input.sessionID`; no usable id under handoff/hard pressure or a hot deny store ⇒ fail closed. Depth signal: the existing in-process tracker (lib/build-gate.mjs `tracker.depth(sessionID)`); that tracker is also the natural home for D1 process-sticky deny. OpenCode may declare `@adlc/context-handoff` as a real dependency and import it directly (the host loads it as an npm package). Also honour the dormant `permission.ask` lever the same way rails-guard does.

**Step 4 — Pi (in-process extension).**
Wire the handoff gate into the tool-execution guard in plugins/adlc-pi/lib/extension.mjs (the same site as the existing rail / build-gate / shell denials), denying mutating tools and shell under the deny-set. Pi exposes a REAL context-fill percentage via `ctx.getContextUsage()` — feed it to `evaluateBands` as the `pct` signal (this is the first adapter to supply pct; depth/bytes stay optional and the OR-join ignores missing kinds; see plugins/adlc-pi/lib/build-gate.mjs for the usage object's shape). Pi has no host-supplied session id: derive a stable per-process session id at `session_start`, document the source, and fail closed for mutations once handoff/hard pressure applies or the deny store is hot if none can be derived.

=== NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR (all three, per spec) ===
1. Gate evaluation goes through `@adlc/context-handoff` (`loadDenyRecords` → `mutationGateInputFromLoad` → `evaluateMutationGate`). No adapter re-declares D1, D2, D3, `authorized()`, or the deny-set.
2. When the absolute **handoff** band fires (`evaluateBands` + `handoffDenyActive`), `ensureDenyMarker` for the current session; an ensure failure is process-sticky deny, never a silent allow.
3. Under the deny-set (D1|D2|D3): deny structured edits AND **Shell/Bash fail-closed-all** (no classifier fork in v1), including agent shell attempts at `adlc handoff write|resume|bypass|repair|unlock`.
4. Protect from agent writes: `.adlc/handoffs/denies/**`, `.adlc/.deny-store`, and `*.resume-auth.json` / `*.model-ok` / `*.lock` under `.adlc/handoffs/`.
5. Fail-open vs fail-closed is asserted in tests in both directions: a clean ADLC repo with no deny store and no band pressure stays fully editable; unreadable input, unresolvable package, unreadable signal, or missing session id under pressure denies.
6. Contract tests drive the **real** harness entrypoint (Codex: the hook script as a subprocess; OpenCode: the exported plugin factory's `tool.execute.before`; Pi: the exported extension's tool event), never a re-implementation of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `@adlc/context-handoff` exports the shared adapter core (`evaluateHandoffPreToolUse`, `isProtectedHandoffPath`, `isHandoffMutatingShell`, `resolveHandoffSessionId`, `HANDOFF_MUTATING_SUBCOMMANDS`). verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/adapter-core.test.mjs`
- The CC adapter delegates to the promoted core instead of holding a second copy, and the frozen slice-4 contract test passes unmodified. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs && git diff --quiet origin/main -- plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Codex denies structured edits under an open deny record belonging to another session with no valid resume-auth. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Codex fail-closes Bash/exec wholesale under the deny-set, including `adlc handoff repair|write|bypass`. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Codex hooks.json wires the handoff hook on the existing PreToolUse mutation matcher (asserted against the shipped hooks.json, not a fixture). verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- The Codex copy of handoff-resolve.mjs is pinned to the CC original by a drift test. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-drift.test.mjs`
- OpenCode aborts edit and bash tool calls under the deny-set via `tool.execute.before`, keyed on `input.sessionID`. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Pi denies mutating tools and shell under the deny-set and derives the band from `ctx.getContextUsage()` as the `pct` signal. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Each of the three adapters writes a deny marker at `.adlc/handoffs/denies/<session_id>.json` when the handoff band fires. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Each of the three adapters allows normally in a clean ADLC repo (no deny store, no band pressure) and fails closed when no usable session id exists under pressure. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- No band/threshold literals appear in the three adapters shipped here — thresholds resolve only through `@adlc/context-handoff`. The check scans the runtime sources of plugins/adlc-codex, plugins/adlc-opencode and plugins/adlc-pi (excluding their test directories) and fails on any occurrence of the band default values (50/60/80 for pct, 20/30/40 for depth, 131072/196608/262144 or the `N * 1024` spellings for bytes) or of a locally declared `HANDOFF_*` / `HARD_*` threshold identifier; it must also prove it bites by asserting a fixture string containing such a literal is rejected. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/no-adapter-threshold-literals.test.mjs`
- Pi still publishes a clean runtime surface after the new files land. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/packaging.test.mjs`
- The Codex integration page documents the enforcing handoff deny. verify: `rg -q 'context-handoff' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/codex.mdx`
- The OpenCode integration page documents the enforcing handoff deny. verify: `rg -q 'context-handoff' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/opencode.mdx`
- The Pi integration page documents the enforcing handoff deny. verify: `rg -q 'context-handoff' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/pi.mdx`
- Binding specs untouched and lint clean. verify: `adlc spec-lint docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md && git diff --quiet origin/main -- docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md .adlc/specs/context-rot-handoff.md`
- Slice 1-4 rails still green. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/cli-test/*.test.mjs packages/build-gate/test/depth-signal.test.mjs packages/build-gate/test/hard-band-compat.test.mjs`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`

allow-suppression: none

Out of scope: Cursor / Gemini(Antigravity) / Copilot adapters and the advisory disclosure-only path (slice 6); Proven CI and harness-attested tool_calls (slice 7); the herdr plugin; repo-wide band-literal ban CI (#474); Gemini depth-50 alignment (#473); changing HARD_*/HANDOFF_* defaults; host compactors; build-gate migration (slice 3, shipped).
title: context-handoff slice 5: enforcing-tier adapters (Codex, OpenCode, Pi) + shared adapter core
